candidate_sources.docs/host-api.md: createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled. Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.

checkpoints: A burst of edits to one open document produces no store write before 120 ms of quiet and exactly one write afterward containing the latest text.
Each new edit in a burst resets the 120 ms quiet interval.
After one burst saves, a later burst for the same document also saves.
Editing with no current view remains a no-op.
Pending edits remain associated with the document that was current when each edit was accepted.
Switching documents, reopening a document, closing, and disposing preserve accepted edits and existing synchronous persistence/navigation behavior.
A save that synchronously calls open or close leaves the nested navigation authoritative; stale outer work does not install or render a superseded view.
Each retired Badge subscription is stopped once, and status rendering remains filtered to its document.
Search preview retains its 40 ms trailing behavior and hide cancellation.
Public createWorkspace/createCoordinator-facing open, edit, close, and dispose interfaces remain unchanged.
forbidden_effects: Do not write to the store directly on every edit.
Do not redirect pending text to whichever document happens to be current when the timer fires.
Do not cancel or lose an accepted document edit merely because its current Badge is retired.
Do not allow a save callback's synchronous nested navigation to be overwritten by stale outer open, close, render, or view installation work.
Do not retain retired Badge subscriptions or deliver another document's status through them.
Do not change store event identity, text, revision, synchronous notification semantics, or document rendering semantics beyond delayed/coalesced persistence.
Do not change createSearchPreview timing, query behavior, or hide cancellation.
Do not change tests, configuration, dependencies, or public interfaces.
lifecycle_identity: Each document ID identifies one reusable BufferBank trailing task, independent of the currently displayed Badge.
The current view/Badge owns the live store subscription and references the buffer for its document; retiring the Badge does not destroy the document-owned buffer.
An edit is bound at acceptance time to the current view's document ID and buffer.
The coordinator request counter identifies the currently authoritative open/close operation across synchronous reentry.
Store status events retain their original id, text, and revision fields.

obligations.text: Replace per-keystroke persistence in the editor edit path with pushing the text into the current view's document buffer; editing without a current view remains a no-op.
Use the existing trailing utility with a 120 ms interval so each burst writes only its latest text after 120 ms without another edit, while allowing subsequent bursts and empty-string edits to save.
Reuse BufferBank entries by document ID so pending work retains its original document association independently of later navigation and Badge lifetime.

Preserve accepted edits and the editor's existing persistence behavior across open replacement, same-document reopen, close, and dispose; any required departure flush must operate on the captured departing buffer without transferring ownership to the destination view.

Before callback-capable saving, consumed pending state must already be retired so synchronous reentry cannot consume the same value twice and edits accepted during the callback can form a later burst.

Retire the old current view and its captured subscription, render the cleared document state, and preserve the request-generation check so synchronous navigation during saving cannot be overwritten by stale outer open work.
Preserve document rendering, store reads and writes, synchronous subscription delivery, status filtering by document ID, and cleanup behavior except for the requested edit coalescing.
Leave createSearchPreview unchanged, including its distinct 40 ms quiet interval and hide cancellation.
Preserve the existing public interfaces exposed for workspace open, edit, close, and dispose.

ordering_barriers: When edit(text) is accepted, read the current view and select that view's buffer before later navigation can change the current view.
On a new edit in the same burst, cancel the prior timer before scheduling the new 120 ms timer.
When flushing, snapshot the pending value and clear/cancel pending state before calling env.store.write, because store listeners may navigate synchronously.
When retiring a view, revoke current-view ownership and capture the old view before invoking callback-capable persistence or cleanup work.
Stop the captured old subscription and complete the old-document clearing effect without later allowing stale outer work to clear or replace a nested successor.

After retirement or any save capable of synchronous navigation, compare the captured open request with the current request before installing a subscription, view, or document render for the requested destination.
preservation: Preserve synchronous Store read/write/subscribe behavior and existing event payload fields.
Preserve document IDs and the exact text supplied by edits, including empty strings.
Preserve independent reusable per-document buffers and live-subscription ownership by the current Badge.
Preserve current-document status filtering and subscription cleanup.
Preserve renderDocument(null) on retirement and renderDocument({id,text:env.store.read(id)}) semantics for an authoritative open.
Preserve open, edit, close, and dispose public behavior and signatures.
Preserve Vue teardown through beforeDestroy calling api.dispose().
Preserve search preview's separate 40 ms trailing task and hide cancellation.

Volunteer coordination — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: separate BufferBank service

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled. Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }

const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));
  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};

triggers: A workspace edit(text) call while a current view exists.
Expiration of the current document buffer's 120 ms quiet timer.
A later edit arriving before that timer expires.
Opening another document or reopening the same document while an edit is pending.
Closing or disposing while an edit is pending.
A synchronous store listener navigating during a timer-driven or departure-driven save.
Vue component destruction invoking coordinator disposal.
